new_sources.title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?
new_sources.artifacts: Authors release 117 papers with code/logs, 351 artifact-aware reviews, SAR scores, human inspections, and configurable harness.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Give reviewers read-only access to the actual experiment workspace and require them to reconcile manuscript numbers against results.json/logs, confirm source code exists and matches the claimed method, verify figures derive from real results, and independently look up references. Treat concrete artifact/reference integrity violations as automatic rejection rather than averaging them into a generic manuscript-quality score. Keep the review workspace immutable so verification cannot silently rewrite the evidence under review.
quantitative_evidence: 117 papers were generated across 13 computer-science seeds, 3 agents, and 3 trials per agent-domain pair; every paper received 3 artifact-aware reviews (351 total) plus manuscript-only SAR and human integrity inspection.
Artifact-aware review lowered mean scores relative to manuscript-only SAR by 0.85 points for Claude Code, 0.42 for Codex, and 0.86 for Kimi Code.
Human audit found paper-vs-artifact mismatch / fabricated-reference rates of 5% / 8% for Codex, 31% / 36% for Claude Code, and 77% / 72% for Kimi Code.
Underpowered-experiment rates were 25.6% Claude Code, 41.0% Codex, 82.1% Kimi Code; plan/execution mismatch was 17.9%, 20.5%, and 33.3% respectively.

Manuscript-only SAR weakly separated the same 200 human ICLR 2025 accepted/rejected papers: mean gap 0.25 points (5.59 vs 5.34) versus the human-review gap 1.52 points (6.54 vs 5.02). SAR manually inferred acceptance was 76% on human-accepted papers but also 52% on human-rejected papers.
None of the 117 agent-generated papers reached the paper's artifact-aware top-tier acceptance bar.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Artifact-aware reviewers were still LLM agents and the paper explicitly says both SAR and PR can over-credit agent-generated work relative to humans. PR is not a deterministic scientific oracle; its strongest contribution is access to immutable artifacts plus explicit integrity checks. Human meta-review focused on objectively checkable integrity rather than novelty. Cross-agent author comparisons are not controlled model-only experiments because agent/model behavior differs broadly.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O: evaluation of a research result should inspect the immutable code/log/result artifacts that generated the claim, not only a polished report or summary. Integrity violations should be typed separately and allowed to block claim promotion. This is a more concrete external implementation of O's context-to-action and evidence-validity concerns than manuscript-only LLM judging.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Use self-refinement selectively by stage rather than assuming recursive critique is uniformly beneficial. Measure whether a revision loop improves the relevant gate and stop/replace it where revisions are neutral or degradative.
quantitative_evidence: Across revision rounds, Claude Code idea self-refinement improved 100% with mean +2.1 and experiment refinement improved 88% with mean +2.2, but paper refinement improved only 43%, stayed same 34%, worsened 23%, mean delta 0.0.
Codex idea refinement improved 35% (mean +0.4), experiment 78% (+2.0), paper 64% (+1.5).
Kimi Code idea refinement improved 100% (+3.0), experiment 91% (+2.2), paper 61% (+1.6).
Self-refinement consumed only about 3%–8% of total wall-clock time, while experiments consumed 67%–83%.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Scores are the framework's stage-gate scores, not external scientific endpoints; revision rounds are triggered below threshold and are not randomized no-refinement controls. The result supports stage heterogeneity, not a causal guarantee that refinement itself improves true research quality.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Medium-high: O should treat critique/revision as a falsifiable local operator whose usefulness can differ by stage. Avoid spending cycles on report/paper polishing when evidence generation or experimental design remains the binding bottleneck.

candidate_mechanisms.description: When research quality is limited by experimental design rather than hardware, additional compute can fail to improve artifact-grounded research quality. Use matched resource-scaling diagnostics before attributing poor outcomes to compute scarcity.
quantitative_evidence: All 8 GPU seeds were rerun with Codex on 8×H100 under a budget matched to the 1×A6000 runs; average artifact-aware PR score decreased from 4.50/4.51 to 4.26 (about -0.24) rather than improving consistently.
Per-domain deltas ranged from +0.22 to -1.00, with no consistent scaling benefit.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: One agent/model, eight GPU-domain seeds, budget-matched ResearchArena setup. It does not show compute is never useful; it shows more hardware was not the binding constraint for these tested research tasks.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High for expected-time optimization: before increasing expensive execution resources, test whether the bottleneck is research design/evidence quality. More parallel compute should not be assumed to compensate for weak experiment selection or plan/execution control.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Claude Code's manuscript-only SAR mean (5.45) looked comparable to the weighted-average human ICLR submission (5.42), yet artifact-aware scores dropped and none of the 117 papers reached the artifact-aware top-tier bar. Manuscript presentation therefore substantially overstated scientific readiness in the tested setup.
new_failure_evidence.scope: ResearchArena's three agents and its SAR/PR/human review design.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O should not use generated report quality, reviewer eloquence, or manuscript-like coherence as a proxy for evidence quality.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Across all 117 papers, mean artifact-aware review score given by Codex was 2.89, Claude Code 3.95, and Kimi Code 5.69, a 2.8-point spread; reviewer effects dominated self-favoring patterns.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Three reviewer agents/models in ResearchArena; not a calibrated error-covariance study and not an external truth ranking.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Raw evaluator scores are not portable across evaluator identities. O should calibrate reviewer severity/validity against external endpoints rather than compare scores from different evaluator configurations as if they share one scale.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Kimi Code planned the most experiments (13.2/trial) and had the highest plan/execution mismatch (33.3%) and underpowered rate (82.1%); Codex planned only 5.7/trial, reduced mismatch to 20.5% but remained underpowered 41.0%. Claude Code was intermediate at 10.6 planned experiments with 17.9% mismatch and 25.6% underpowered.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Descriptive cross-agent comparison; agent/model identity confounds planning style with other capabilities.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Research planning needs capacity-aware task contracts and post-plan feasibility checks; merely making plans larger or smaller is not enough.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Budget-matched H100 scaling for Codex did not improve average artifact-aware quality and slightly reduced it.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Eight ResearchArena GPU seeds for Codex.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Diagnose bottleneck class before spending compute; resource scaling can be low-value when experimental design is the limiting factor.

synthesis_with_prior_records.observation: ResearchArena provides a direct scientist-agent counterpart to BadScientist: manuscript-only review can look favorable while artifact inspection exposes missing/fabricated evidence. It also complements ScientistOne and EviGraph by showing a practical reviewer implementation that reads immutable code/log/results, and complements scBench-Long by reinforcing that evaluator/reviewer configuration is part of the tested system rather than a neutral measurement wrapper.
synthesis_with_prior_records.novel_relative_to_O: The strongest new asymmetry is not the generic idea of provenance, which O already knows, but the measured magnitude of paper-vs-artifact failures, the explicit read-only artifact-review procedure, stage-specific self-refinement effectiveness, and matched hardware-scaling null result.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not treat ResearchArena PR as a perfect oracle; the authors explicitly say artifact-aware LLM review can still over-credit agent-generated work versus humans.
Do not infer Claude Code is generally superior to Codex/Kimi from these results; agent/model/scaffolding behavior is confounded and the paper measures this particular configuration.
Do not interpret H100 non-improvement as evidence that compute is never useful; only that it was not the binding constraint in the tested eight Codex GPU seeds.
Do not infer self-refinement causality from stage-score deltas alone because revisions were threshold-triggered rather than randomized against no-refinement controls.
Do not count triple-reviewer mean as independent evidence without dependence calibration; prior record 008 shows nominal reviewer count can substantially overstate effective independence.
next_queries: Inspect the separate 2026 ResearchArena sabotage/control benchmark (arXiv:2607.19321) for controlled evidence on executable artifact probing versus trajectory-only monitoring and failure modes of artifact-aware monitors.
Find controlled artifact-aware-review ablations: manuscript-only vs static artifacts vs executable probing vs deterministic checks, with human/external ground truth.
Find research-agent interventions that reduce underpowered experiments or plan/execution mismatch through capacity-aware contracts, preflight feasibility, or adaptive replanning.
Find stage-specific self-refinement randomized ablations that measure downstream research endpoint rather than internal gate score.
Continue matched same-vs-cross-model scientific reviewer, evaluator-covariance, memory-applicability, and specification-validation searches.
